title: The Greeks
objectives: Define delta, gamma, theta, vega and rho.
Interpret the signs for long options.
body_md:
The **Greeks** measure the sensitivity of premium to its inputs.

| Greek | Sensitivity to | Long call | Long put |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Delta** | Spot price | 0 to +1 | −1 to 0 |
| **Gamma** | Change in delta | Positive | Positive |
| **Theta** | Time passing | Negative | Negative |
| **Vega** | Volatility | Positive | Positive |
| **Rho** | Interest rate | Positive | Negative |

## Reading them

- **Delta** also approximates the probability of finishing ITM; ATM options are near 0.5.
- **Gamma** is highest for ATM options close to expiry.
- **Theta** (time decay) hurts buyers and helps sellers; it speeds up near expiry.
- **Vega** is highest for ATM options with more time to expiry.

## Delta hedging

Holding delta-neutral positions removes small price risk; it needs constant adjustment because gamma changes delta.

Example: a call with delta 0.6: if spot rises ₹1, premium rises about ₹0.60.

> **Exam tip:** Long options have positive gamma and vega, negative theta.
example: A trader holds 10 lots of calls with delta 0.5 and lot size 100. Position delta = 10 × 100 × 0.5 = 500 shares equivalent.
